title: Transfer of ringed-site resolving tensor localization across an exact equivalence
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with symmetric monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with symmetry $\beta_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\otimes X$ natural in both variables, with $\beta_{Y,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y}=\mathrm{id}$ and the hexagon identity $\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\beta_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(\beta_{X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Z)$, with countable coproducts and tensor additive and preserving those coproducts in each variable. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and homotopy categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and signed direct-sum total tensors [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Flatness means tensor exactness, and K-flatness means the equivalent acyclic-tensor and two-sided quasi-isomorphism tests; on $\mathcal M$ use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex].
Suppose $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal A$ and $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal M$ are additive exact quasi-inverse equivalences, equipped with coherent strong monoidal comparisons [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] that are symmetric: the inverse tensorator $c_{X,Y}:F(X\otimes Y)\cong FX\otimes FY$ satisfies $c_{Y,X}\circ F(\beta_{X,Y})=\beta_{FX,FY}\circ c_{X,Y}$, and $G$ carries the inverse comparisons. Suppose their termwise functors preserve and reflect flat objects and K-flat complexes, and have specified coherent signed-total comparisons $\tau_{P,Q}:F_{\rm Ch}(P\otimes Q)\cong F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes F_{\rm Ch}Q$, inverse for $G$.
Write $\mathcal P_R\subset K(\mathcal M)$ and $\mathcal P_{\mathcal A}\subset K(\mathcal A)$ for the full subcategories of flat-term K-flat complexes, $W_R,W_{\mathcal A}$ for their quasi-isomorphisms, and $Q_R,Q_{\mathcal A}$ for the homotopy-to-derived localizations. Then the termwise unit and counit induce mutually inverse equivalences $D(F),D(G)$, and $W_{\mathcal A}^{-1}\mathcal P_{\mathcal A}\to D(\mathcal A)$ is an equivalence. The total tensor on $\mathcal A$ induces its ordinary unbounded K-flat derived tensor with canonical model maps $m_{\mathcal A;P,Q}:Q_{\mathcal A}(P\otimes Q)\cong Q_{\mathcal A}P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_{\mathcal A}Q$. Let $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and $m_{R;P,Q}:Q_R(P\otimes_RQ)\cong Q_RP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_RQ$ ($P,Q\in\mathcal P_R$) be the ringed-site derived tensor and its canonical model isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and $\kappa_P:D(F)Q_RP\cong Q_{\mathcal A}F_{\rm Ch}P$ the exact-functor localization comparison.
There is a natural isomorphism $t_{K,L}:D(F)(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\cong D(F)K\otimes^{\mathbf L}D(F)L$, uniquely determined on flat-term K-flat $P,Q$ by
$$(\kappa_P\otimes\kappa_Q)\circ t_{Q_RP,Q_RQ}\circ D(F)(m_{R;P,Q})=m_{\mathcal A;FP,FQ}\circ Q_{\mathcal A}(\tau_{P,Q})\circ\kappa_{P\otimes Q}.$$
This comparison and the localized ordinary unit comparison respect associators, both unitors and the native Koszul symmetries. The same formula computes $t$ on any K-flat representatives, even without flat terms, using their K-flat tensor model comparisons; it agrees with any independently specified ordinary K-flat derived tensor carrying these model maps. No functorial choice of resolutions in $\mathcal A$ is required.

proof.text: For every target complex apply the independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem to its inverse image. Apply the forward exact functor to the resulting quasi-isomorphism and compose with the termwise counit. Flatness and K-flatness transfer by hypothesis. The existing restriction-localization theorem, proved using refinements of fractions, makes the flat-term target homotopy subcategory a localization. Its abstract localization is therefore equivalent to the target derived category.

proof.text: The source TensorModel makes its restricted complex-to-derived functor strong monoidal and braided: use the inverses of the model pair and unit isomorphisms. The supplied total comparison makes the restricted termwise equivalence strong monoidal and braided. Transport the source localization functor along this equivalence and the exact-functor factorization isomorphism. This constructs a strong monoidal and braided localization on all target K-flat complexes. Its inverse tensorator and inverse unit are the target model maps. Monoidal functor laws prove all TensorModel fields. K-flat units and products are closed directly by the unitors and associator applied to the two-sided quasi-isomorphism test.

proof.text: The monoidality equation for the exact-functor localization isomorphism, inverted, is exactly the prescribed tensor normalization on every K-flat pair. Its unit equation gives precisely the localized ordinary unit comparison. The transported derived equivalence is braided, giving the native symmetry equation. For uniqueness, apply two-variable localization extensionality to the source flat-term K-flat homotopy localization. On representatives cancel the invertible source model map and the tensor of factorization comparisons; the two normalization equations then coincide.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat; agent-written transfer of the resolving-localization and coherent derived comparison argument to an exactly equivalent coefficient category.

proof.text: For any independently specified target TensorModel, descend each model strong monoidal localization to the full K-flat homotopy subcategory; fullness of the homotopy quotient descends naturality, and its native associator and unitor equations descend coherence. This subcategory localizes by the target replacements constructed above. Apply Mathlib Localization.Monoidal.functorCoreMonoidalOfComp to the identity functor, using the old model on the source localization and the new model on its lift. This constructs the identity comparison. Its unit and tensor maps compute to the new model inverse followed by the old model. The symmetry equation follows on K-flat representatives from the symmetry laws of the two models and then on every object by essential surjectivity. Compose the old normalized tensor comparison with the inverse tensorator of this identity comparison. Oplax monoidal naturality and the model formula show that this composite is normalized for the new model. The uniqueness argument just proved identifies it with every independently normalized comparison.
